Expressing Unfulfilled Plans: Past Perfect with Before and For
When you planned to do something and did not do it, you call this an unfulfilled plan.

You use the Past Perfect to talk about unfulfilled plans.

The Past Perfect expresses the idea that something did or did not occur before another action in the past. It can also show that something did or did not happen before a specific time in the past.

For example:

I had intended to make a presentation on careers in communications, but it was canceled due to lack of enrollment.

I had expected many people to participate, but they did not register in time.

You use the words before and for with the Past Perfect.

You use before to refer to the more ‘past' action (the action that happened first).

I had hoped to talk to her before I wrote this letter, but she appears to be very busy.

You use the preposition for to talk about how long an action lasted.

For example:

I had wanted to meet a headhunter for over a month.
I had planned on leaving early, but I was held up at work.
We had both wanted to apply for the job, but it was already filled.
They had wanted to go to the conference, but they couldn't take the time off.
Modals for Expressing Necessity: Must and Mustn't
You use the modal must to talk about necessity - when it is imperative that something is done.

Must can sound quite serious and is most commonly used in writing. Native speakers prefer the more flexible form have to when speaking.

For example:

You must keep trying.
Young people today must ask for help to secure a good job.
You use must not to talk about prohibited actions. It is common to read must not in rules, laws and regulations.

** Pronunciation tip:

When pronouncing the contracted form of must not (mustn't), you pronounce it as mussint.
Practice saying these sentences:

You mustn't give up on your job search.
You mustn't feel alone.
You use need not (needn't) when you want to refer to something that is not necessary.
You must fill out this application and send it in.
You mustn't wait until the last moment to do do it.
You must ask them to notify you.

images.text:
Dear Mr. Bari,

Thank you very much for your e-mail introducing yourself. Ms Sanders told me about your situation. I had hoped to talk to her before I wrote this letter, but she appears to be very busy.
I am most interested in helping young people who want to enter the field of communications start their career. I imagine you have experienced difficulty finding a job in this competitive field. I expect you have been through many interviews, without a great deal of success.

My guess is that you have struggled to find interesting job postings, to no avail. I understand all these problems. That's why the services of a headhunter are so essential for young people in today's job market. You must keep trying. You mustn't give up on your job search.
Let me assure you that a headhunter such as myself can be a great help in your job search. You needn't feel alone. Young people today need help to secure a good job.

In addition to recommending employment opportunities, I could help you to grow your network of contacts and give you strategies for building your online presence. We can set up a meeting to discuss different opportunities.
I had intended to make a presentation on careers in communications, but it was canceled due to lack of enrollment. I had expected many people to participate, but they did not register in time.
Please contact my office by telephone for a follow-up meeting.

Regards,

Andrew Goldstein
